keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «크리스퍼는 예전 방법보다 더 빠르고 싸고 훨씬 정확하다(장점)» 와 «유전자 편집은 병을 고칠 수 있는 강력한 도구지만 분명한 윤리 규칙에 따라 신중하게 써야 한다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the strength (CRISPR is faster, cheaper, and far more precise than older methods) and the conclusion (gene editing is a powerful tool, but it must be used carefully with clear ethical rules). The green sentences are the answers.

sum.pre: Every living cell contains DNA, a long molecule that carries the
code. CRISPR is a tool that can cut DNA at a chosen
, and it is faster, cheaper, and more
than older methods. A treatment for sickle cell disease has already been approved. However, editing human
is strongly debated, because those changes would be passed on to future
. Therefore, gene editing must be used carefully and with clear ethical rules.

qs.q: Why do many countries strictly limit changes to human embryos?
qs.qko: 많은 나라가 사람 배아를 바꾸는 일을 엄격하게 제한하는 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Because those changes would be passed on to future generations
Because CRISPR cannot cut DNA at all
Because embryos are too small to study
evs: The biggest debate concerns editing human embryos, because those changes would be passed on to future generations.
Since then, the technology has been used to develop crops that resist disease and to study illnesses in the lab.
Compared with older methods, CRISPR is faster, cheaper, and far more precise.
Sometimes a tiny error in this code causes serious diseases.
why: 본문에 배아를 편집하면 그 변화가 다음 세대로 전해지기 때문에 가장 큰 논쟁거리라고 나와요. 그래서 많은 나라가 엄격하게 제한하거나 금지해요.
Changes to human embryos would be passed on to future generations, which is why this is the biggest debate.

qs.q: In the text, what are "off-target effects"?
opts: Cuts made in the wrong place, which could cause new health problems
Treatments that cost too much for most people
Crops that resist disease very well
evs: Cuts in the wrong place, known as off-target effects, could cause new health problems.
In 2012, researchers including Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier showed how a tool called CRISPR-Cas9 could cut DNA at a chosen spot.
Compared with older methods, CRISPR is faster, cheaper, and far more precise.
Sometimes a tiny error in this code causes serious diseases.
why: 본문에서 잘못된 곳을 자르는 것을 «off-target effects» 라고 한다고 해요. 원하지 않은 엉뚱한 곳을 자르면 새로운 건강 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
The text says cuts in the wrong place are known as off-target effects, and they could cause new health problems.

qs.q: Why was the 2018 experiment in China so strongly criticized?
qs.qko: 2018년 중국의 실험은 왜 그렇게 강하게 비판받았나요?
opts: He edited the genes of twin babies, and embryo changes pass to future generations
He used an old method that was slower than CRISPR
He refused to share his results with other scientists
evs: In 2018, a scientist in China announced that he had edited the genes of twin babies, and researchers around the world strongly criticized the experiment.
The biggest debate concerns editing human embryos, because those changes would be passed on to future generations.
For their work, Doudna and Charpentier received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020.
Since then, the technology has been used to develop crops that resist disease and to study illnesses in the lab.
why: 중국의 한 과학자가 쌍둥이 아기의 유전자를 편집했다고 발표했는데, 배아의 변화는 다음 세대로 전해지기 때문에 가장 큰 논쟁거리예요. 두 단서를 이어 보면 왜 세계의 연구자들이 강하게 비판했는지 알 수 있어요.
A scientist edited the genes of twin babies, and changes to embryos would be passed on to future generations. Together, these clues explain the strong criticism.
